\section*{Provenance of every quoted number}

Each tag used in the main text resolves to a file in this repository. "line N" means the value can be read literally at that line of the archived standard output; those stdout files live under \texttt{evidence/**}, are tracked, and are hash-listed under \texttt{evidence/*/MANIFEST.sha256}; they were not re-typed by hand. \texttt{nlcsplit/logs/} is a different case and is stated as such rather than glossed: only three sidecar JSONs there are tracked (\texttt{step\_h.json}, \texttt{step\_h\_l2cp.json}, \texttt{orca\_anchor.json}), the rest of that directory ignores \texttt{*.out} by its own \texttt{.gitignore}, so a run log left there is a working note and not evidence.

Row 0 is therefore homonuclear and labelled as the archived run labels it, and it reproduces the reference cross term and the package cross term with a difference of exactly 0.000e+00 - which is what licenses the three unequal-centre rows. S24 & \texttt{nlcsplit/step\_m\_ccsdt.py}, \texttt{evidence/\allowbreak{}ccsdt/\allowbreak{}20260930T224400Z\_\allowbreak{}stepm\_\allowbreak{}ladder\_\allowbreak{}after\_\allowbreak{}refactor.out}, \texttt{evidence/\allowbreak{}ccsdt/\allowbreak{}20260930T235900Z\_\allowbreak{}stepm\_\allowbreak{}three\_\allowbreak{}systems\_\allowbreak{}631g.out}, \texttt{evidence/\allowbreak{}ccsdt/\allowbreak{}20261001T000400Z\_\allowbreak{}stepm\_\allowbreak{}three\_\allowbreak{}systems\_\allowbreak{}avdz.out}, \texttt{evidence/\allowbreak{}ccsdt/\allowbreak{}20260930T212300Z\_\allowbreak{}stepm\_\allowbreak{}ladder.out}, \texttt{evidence/\allowbreak{}ccsdt/\allowbreak{}20261001T044833Z\_\allowbreak{}orca\_\allowbreak{}crosscheck.out}, \texttt{evidence/\allowbreak{}ccsdt/\allowbreak{}20261001T052943Z\_\allowbreak{}orca\_\allowbreak{}crosscheck\_\allowbreak{}three\_\allowbreak{}systems.out}, \texttt{evidence/\allowbreak{}ccsdt/\allowbreak{}orca\_\allowbreak{}crosscheck.py}, \texttt{evidence/ccsdt/README.md}, \texttt{evidence/\allowbreak{}ccsdt/\allowbreak{}MANIFEST.sha256}, \texttt{nlcsplit/\allowbreak{}tests/\allowbreak{}test\_\allowbreak{}cc\_\allowbreak{}convention.py}, \texttt{evidence/\allowbreak{}ccsdt/\allowbreak{}20261003T0703Z\_\allowbreak{}stepm\_\allowbreak{}water\_\allowbreak{}fivebases\_\allowbreak{}ghostcp\_\allowbreak{}local.out} & the coupled-cluster anchor for the water-dimer binding energy: same official S22 geometry, same basis, same counterpoise convention, RHF reference, MP2/CCSD/CCSD(T) from PySCF's own modules, each rung reported both frozen-core and all-electron. The archive also records the mixed-convention bug this run nearly shipped with: freezing the monomers while switching only the dimer's convention printed -23.16 kcal/mol for the water dimer, which is impossible, and the impossibility was 17 kcal of oxygen 1s correlation counted on one side of the difference only. Two runs are kept because the second one exists to prove the first is still valid: after the frozen-core selection was refactored into a single call feeding both sides of the difference, the ladder was re-run with the script as it now ships, and stripped of wall-clock columns the two files differ in five lines, all of them one print statement whose wording changed - no energy moved. \texttt{nlcsplit/\allowbreak{}tests/\allowbreak{}test\_\allowbreak{}cc\_\allowbreak{}convention.py} pins that invariant, and one of its seven tests rebuilds the broken pairing on purpose to show the guard can fail. \texttt{evidence/\allowbreak{}ccsdt/\allowbreak{}orca\_\allowbreak{}crosscheck.py} is the third-program check: ORCA 6.0.1, same geometries, same basis, same convention, on three systems and both conventions (eight rows, 24 single points), worst difference 0.0002 kcal/mol on the interaction energy and 1.2e-07 Ha between executions on the absolute energies. \textbf{What that check validated has to be restated:} it built its monomers the way the script of the day built them, so both programs were computing the \emph{uncorrected} difference and agreeing about it - a cross-program check on a convention proves nothing about the convention when both sides share the same omission, which is why the corrected check is constructed from the definition instead of mirrored from the other script. The corrected comparison, with ghost functions on both sides and the basis dimension read back per part, is \prov{S30}. \texttt{evidence/\allowbreak{}ccsdt/\allowbreak{}20261001T052943Z\_\allowbreak{}orca\_\allowbreak{}crosscheck\_\allowbreak{}three\_\allowbreak{}systems.out} is the one to cite for it; it also carries the correction of an earlier claim in this directory, which is why the basis check is stated the way it is. The first version of that check read ORCA's \texttt{Number of basis functions} field against PySCF's orbital count and reported agreement at 18 for a water monomer in 6-31G* - true, but not a criterion: for the same monomer in aug-cc-pVDZ the field prints 47 while ORCA's own SCF and coupled-cluster sections print \texttt{Basis Dimension Dim .... 41} and \texttt{Number of AO's ... 41}, which is PySCF's number. So the script now reads back the AO dimension per part and compares it with the PySCF nao for the same geometry and basis (24/24 equal), and its verdict refuses to print "agree" unless the energy test and the basis test hold at the same time. The 47 itself is recorded as unexplained rather than rationalised: 25 shells with maximum angular momentum 2 admits no s/p/d/sp bookkeeping that yields both 47 and 41. The frozen-core convention of each ORCA run is likewise read from its own output (\texttt{chemical core (4 el)} on a dimer, \texttt{(2 el)} on a monomer, \texttt{NO frozen core} on the all-electron rungs) rather than assumed from the input keyword. \textbf{Dated correction, 2026-10-03:} the column headed \texttt{dE\_CP} in the four ladder archives named above is \emph{not} a counterpoise value - the monomers were built in their own basis, so the partner's functions were absent. \prov{S30} gives the corrected ladders, the row-by-row proof that only the monomer side moved between the two sets of archives, and the size of what the mismatch was worth (0.2518-2.9711 kcal/mol per complex). The row is kept because it is the record of what those runs computed, and because the correction is the point of \S{}3.2's second paragraph \\

One SCF, one grid and one set of weights are held fixed while only the ownership factors vary: the package's own multi-centre factor is evaluated on the common grid's coordinates, normalised point-by-point to sum to one over atoms, and handed to the decomposition function through its soft= path - so the quadrature cannot move and the reported spread is attribution alone. The quadrature side is then read separately, as the totals each scheme produces on its own grid with the same density matrix. Four guards are in the file: every point's soft weights must sum to 1 within 1e-8 or the run exits; the hard nearest-atom assignment on the common grid must reproduce the published census control value (water, -7.8950 kcal/mol, gate 0.005 - the archive prints a difference of 0.0000); the closure check is on throughout, so each block sum is compared against one monolithic evaluation over the same kept points rather than against itself; and the soft= path itself is pinned by nlcsplit/tests/test\_nlc\_closure.py, whose negative controls regroup the blocks so that one cross term is double-counted and then dropped, and require the guard to fire. The same runs print the discrete residual of the local term, beta times (sum W rho minus the electron number), which is the quantity the abstract's cancellation statement is about: -0.0013 to +0.0011 kcal/mol over eight cells at grid level 1. The verdict the file pre-registered before it was run was a two-way one - attribution comparable to or larger than quadrature keeps the name "attribution uncertainty", attribution near zero would have taken that name away - and all eight cells came out on the first side, with the printed ratios spanning 1.29 (methane) to 1046.15 (benzene...water). Two provenance details are kept in the archive rather than smoothed over. The two 24-atom cells ran on a cluster node under a Slurm job, so the header line that records the repository commit is \textbf{empty} - the uploaded tree carries no git metadata - and the commit that produced them is recorded outside the file instead, together with the byte-identical hashes of the three modules the run prints for itself (\texttt{nlcsplit/partition.py}, \texttt{nlcsplit/nlc.py}, \texttt{nlcsplit/step\_h\_s22.py}), which match the ones now shipped and the ones that produced the six smaller cells; what makes those eight cells one comparison is those hashes, not the commit string. And the run's own exit code is kept in a separate rc file because a shared marker got overwritten by a later kill once before. Two things this archive is not. Its water cell reads a pure-attribution span of 0.0433 kcal/mol against the 0.0435 published for the same cell in Table 3, and the difference is the grid, not the density - one number is measured on the common grid with the weights held fixed, the other across the four schemes' own grids. And both filenames carry a host-supplied timestamp rather than the machine's own clock, because the Linux clock on the machine that produced them was three days behind when the first archive was named; \texttt{evidence/\allowbreak{}common\_\allowbreak{}grid/\allowbreak{}NOTE-clock-skew.md} records which name was stamped by which clock and why the bytes were not renamed afterwards \\

Every archive the ladder admits, excludes or splits is named inside the reading file itself, one line each with its byte count and digest, so this column names only the ASCII-spelled ones - seven of the eight level-1 rungs carry the system name in Chinese in their own filenames and pdflatex cannot set them; the reader reaches them from the reading file rather than from here. The gate is 0.005 kcal/mol, the same value the census guardrail prints inside these archives, and it is a constant in the script, not a function of the grid level being tested. Nothing here is trusted on its notification: an archive is admitted only if its own sidecar exit-code file, an in-file exit line, and a success code all agree, which is why 18 archives glob into the directory, 15 are admitted and 3 are excluded and named with the reason (one predates the grid-coordinate fix, two have a sidecar but no in-file exit line). Rungs are grouped by partition-file digest prefix and system, so a coarse reading from one revision of the code can never be joined to a fine reading from another and the pair that produced Table 3's two benzene rows under the pre-merge hash shows up as single-rung, i.e. not measured. Repeated runs at the \emph{same} level are printed as a repeatability line and are explicitly not a convergence rung. Every span the table recomputes is tied out against the span printed in the same file, allowing one unit of the last printed digit: 52 comparisons, maximum deviation 1, none over tolerance - the residual is rounding, and the prose quotes the printed value. Two claims are reported and cannot be quoted for each other. The registered primary one asks whether each ladder is stable over its whole span of levels and answers \textbf{rc=3}, because two ladders exceed the gate on their coarse step (benzene...water 0.0076, benzene dimer (A) 0.0154 from level 0 to 1); that exit code is not softened, and level 0 is not dropped from the ladder to make the table pass. The secondary claim, added after the coarse steps were seen and printed as such, restricts the same gate to the top two rungs and only when both are at or above the published level - a level established by census of the certificate headers in the same directory, every one of which declares the same one, rather than a number typed by whoever wrote the script - and of the eight cells five have such a pair and all five are stable (0.0000, 0.0000, 0.0001, 0.0009, 0.0001); the other three are counted as NOT MEASURED rather than as passes, because their best pair reaches down to level 0 and therefore cannot answer the question. \texttt{evidence/\allowbreak{}common\_\allowbreak{}grid/\allowbreak{}grid\_\allowbreak{}level\_\allowbreak{}convergence\_\allowbreak{}negative\_\allowbreak{}control.py} is the must-fail half of this row: ten cases, each with the exit code the script is required to produce, covering an in-gate ladder, an out-of-gate ladder, a rung with no sidecar exit code, a sidecar exit code that disagrees with its own archive, a truncated archive, a span inconsistent with its own columns, a cross-hash pair, and an empty input set; the last case is an invariant (the verdict code must agree with the number of unstable ladders it printed, and a ladder must exist at all) rather than an expected value read off today's archive set, because a data-dependent expectation implodes the moment a legitimate new rung lands. S15's files were sitting in \texttt{scratch/}, which is gitignored - they were promoted into \texttt{evidence/} on 2026-09-29 for exactly that reason. And one distinction has to be kept: S6 and S13 come from the same CentOS batch timestamped 2026-09-28T16:58, which is earlier than the geometry fix, while S12's primary artefact is a recompute run afterwards. Within that earlier batch the initial S22 structure and the relaxed one are distinguishable (the level-0 6-31G* value -0.5316 appears in S13's ladder, while the -0.5975 of the relaxed structure does not), so S13's cross-grid spreads are read here as measured on the \emph{initial} S22 geometry, not on the relaxed one that carries the headline numbers. The level-1 column of that same ladder agrees with the later recompute to four decimals for all three bases the two runs share, so the grid-convergence conclusion does not turn on which geometry was used - but that was checked after the fact. The full ladder has since been re-run on the geometry that carries the headline numbers, and section 3.4 quotes that run (\texttt{evidence/\allowbreak{}recompute/\allowbreak{}20260930T191014Z\_\allowbreak{}stepg-official.out}); what remains true is the weaker thing: the cross-grid spreads of S13 are still measured on the initial structure, because that is the batch which contains all four grid levels.

\textbf{Hirshfeld cross-check status.} The full-S22 cross-family check is not used as evidence in this paper. Its Hirshfeld column agrees with the older eight-cell archive in four of the eight cells; the other four (\#10, \#11, \#18 and \#20) are reported as NOT MEASURED for equivalence rather than reconciled, and no number in Tables 1-3 or Table S2 depends on that column. Because the column is outside the four-scheme family, its absence cannot move the reported range.

\section*{The nlcsplit package}

This appendix describes the code that produced the numbers above. It is filed here rather than as a separate software manuscript because everything method-shaped in such a manuscript would repeat section 2 and everything result-shaped would repeat section 3, and a second paper would then need a second provenance system to keep the two in step. Everything stated below is checkable from the repository: the entry point by importing it, the release record by reading the archives named in \prov{S37}.

\textbf{Shape.} \texttt{nlcsplit} is pure Python on NumPy and PySCF. No compiled extension is built or required, and those two are the only dependencies. Three modules carry the physics - \texttt{nlcsplit/nlc.py} (the VV10 fields and the blocked pair sum), \texttt{nlcsplit/partition.py} (the attribution schemes) and \texttt{nlcsplit/geomlib.py} (geometries, fragment boundaries derived from covalent connectivity, and the loader for the published S22 geometries). Every table of the manuscript is produced by exactly one \texttt{step\_*.py} script, which writes a JSON sidecar beside its archived standard output, and \texttt{nlcsplit/figures.py} draws only from those sidecars and refuses to draw when one fails to parse. A figure therefore cannot outlive the run that made it, which is the failure mode the whole archive structure exists to prevent.

\textbf{One entry point.} The public surface is a single function:

\texttt{nlc.fragment\_\allowbreak{}decomposition(coords, weights, rho, sigma, fragments, b, C, owner=None, soft=None, rho\_\allowbreak{}floor=1e-12, closure\_\allowbreak{}check=False)}

\texttt{fragments} is a list of atom-index groups. \texttt{owner} gives the index of the atom that owns each grid point - a hard assignment - and \texttt{soft} is an (natm, ngrid) weight matrix whose columns sum to one, as returned by \texttt{partition.scheme\_factors}. The function returns \texttt{E\_loc}, \texttt{E\_nl}, \texttt{E\_total}, \texttt{intra} keyed by fragment and \texttt{inter} keyed by fragment pair, and \texttt{inter[(A, B)]} is the whole cross contribution rather than a half, which is what makes the sum of \texttt{intra} plus the sum of \texttt{inter} equal \texttt{E\_nl} in the first place. \texttt{closure\_check=True} compares that block sum against one monolithic evaluation over the same kept points and raises if they differ; it is off by default because the reference doubles the summation, and section 2.2 states both the residual it gives on the systems reported here and the inputs the check shares with the quantity it audits \prov{S33}. Parameters come from PySCF's \texttt{nlc\_coeff} rather than from constants in this package, so a different VV10 parameterisation cannot silently disagree with the functional that generated the density.

\textbf{Six attributions, one shape.} \texttt{partition.scheme\_\allowbreak{}factors(mol, coords, scheme)} dispatches on the four Becke-family constructions used in the text (\texttt{becke}, \texttt{becke-becke-rad}, \texttt{becke-treutler}, \texttt{stratmann}) and on two cross-family controls (\texttt{voronoi}, \texttt{hirshfeld}). All six return the same array shape, so comparing attributions is a one-keyword change and nothing else moves. Every construction passes the same guard before returning: the pointwise sum of the attribution weights must sit within 1e-12 of one, or the function raises instead of handing back a matrix that would silently mis-normalise the double sum. That figure is an assertion threshold in the shipped code, not a measured residual, and \texttt{nlcsplit/\allowbreak{}tests/\allowbreak{}test\_\allowbreak{}partition\_\allowbreak{}factors.py} is where it is pinned. The two cross-family constructions enter no span quoted in this paper: they are reported separately and are thread-count sensitive, which is recorded in the provenance row for the grid ladder \prov{S34}, and the ranges the text publishes are family-internal by construction.

\textbf{The worked example, run verbatim.} \texttt{nlcsplit/\allowbreak{}examples/\allowbreak{}quickstart.py} on the water dimer at omegaB97X-V/6-31G*, grid level 1, with the Becke partition, prints

\texttt{inter[(0,1)] = -0.5237   intra = -3.5457 -3.7437   E\_\allowbreak{}nl = -7.8130   E\_\allowbreak{}loc = 60.8303   E\_\allowbreak{}total = 53.0172}

in kcal/mol, and the archive of that stdout carries the interpreter version and the SHA-256 of the four modules that produced it \prov{S37}. Two arithmetic points are worth stating rather than skipping, because the printed lines invite the reader to add them: the three block values sum to one unit in the last printed place above the printed \texttt{E\_nl}, and \texttt{E\_nl} plus \texttt{E\_loc} differs from the printed \texttt{E\_total} by the same one unit. Each line rounds independently, and the additivity guard of section 2.2 runs on the doubles rather than on what is printed. \texttt{E\_total} is a different object from the interaction energy of section 3 and must not be read as one; the agreement with the native kernel that the text quotes is the 5.7e-06 kcal/mol of section 2.1, measured on a fixed density and a fixed grid \prov{S5}.

\textbf{Two checks that ship with the package.} Neither is about this paper's conclusions; both are about whether the quantity is what the label says. The first recomputes the nonlocal term for the eight complexes in an external program, ORCA 6.0.1, together with an omegaB97X control that must not print the nonlocal label at all - a gate on the reporting convention rather than on a number \prov{S18}. The second re-evaluates the cross term of a two-Gaussian model density by three independent routes and reports its own error bar, so the attribution can be audited on a system where no real-space partition is involved at all \prov{S22}. The two chemical controls of section 3.4 are ordinary calls of the same pipeline on a dative and an ionic complex [S35, S36], and no new attribution code was written for either.

\textbf{What runs before a release.} The package is Apache-2.0 and contains no GAMESS source. That claim is checked by scanning the files an install actually produces for source artefacts - \texttt{*.src}, \texttt{*.f}, \texttt{*.for}, \texttt{GAMESS*} - rather than by grepping the tree for a word the disclaimer itself contains. The archived scan reports 45 installed files, three named exemptions and no hit outside the exemption ledger at exit code 0 \prov{S37}. Correctness is guarded in the same spirit: the test suite pins the kernel against PySCF's native one, regression-tests the archived numbers, and checks the geometry and partition-factor invariants; the suite collects 94 tests at the revision that census records (71 not marked slow, 23 marked slow), it prints its per-module counts beside their total so that a silently dropped category cannot pass as a member count, and it names the modules that stay out of the wheel with the reason rather than leaving them absent \prov{S37}. Above that, the export tool \texttt{tools/make\_public\_repo.js} enforces fifteen gates over the tree that would actually be published, and one command in the parent repository (\texttt{tools/run\_ship\_qa.sh}) drives it end to end. Each gate carries a two-directional self-test that must fire on a planted fault and stay silent on valid input, and the build refuses to ship when a self-test does not fire - a gate that cannot be made to fail is not a gate. Table S3 lists them with the real defect that put each one there. These are the counts of the archived run named above; the census re-runs against whatever wheel is actually released, so a reader holding a newer build should expect the shipped list to have grown rather than to disagree.

\normalsize

\textbf{Limits of the software.} The pair sum is quadratic in the number of retained grid points and there is no sub-quadratic approximation in the package. One attempt at a certified screening was built, measured and rejected; section 3.6 states the measurement and what it does not license, and the companion screening manuscript carries the raw timings. The implementation is VV10 only - the tau-dependent rVV10 form is not implemented, and the parameters are read from whatever the installed PySCF reports for the functional in use, so a functional whose VV10 parameters PySCF does not expose cannot be evaluated here. And this is not an energy decomposition analysis: it resolves one term of the functional into fragment pairs and says nothing about electrostatics, exchange-repulsion, polarisation or charge transfer, which is why section 4.1 states what the decomposition is not before section 4.2 lets the reader use it.
